description.narrative: The objectives of this contributions are: 1) Develop evidence of high quality to deepen knowledge of poverty reduction. 2) Share evidence strategically to influence decisions. 3) Equip decision makers with evidence to improve living conditions for people living in poverty.

Denna insats ett kärnstöd som bidrar till IPA:s 2025 Strategic Ambitions - organisationens strategiplan för de kommande åren. Insatsen omfattar 40 MSEK under tre år, där aktivitetsperioden är mellan 2023 - 2025. Detta stöd fram har beretts inom ramen för Strategin för kapacitetsutveckling, partnerskap och metoder som stöder Agenda 2030 för hållbar utveckling (KAPAME). Målen med insatsen är: 1) Skapa evidens av hög kvalitet – för att fördjupa kunskapen om fattigdomsminkning. 2) Dela evidens strategiskt – för att påverka beslut. 3) Utrusta beslutsfattare evidens – för att förbättra villkoren för människor som lever i fattigdom.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between The Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, Sida and Innovations for Poverty Action regarding Core Support
Beslut om stöd till Innovations for Poverty Action 2022-2025

description.narrative:
Sida assess that the report covers all essential areas that IPA has been contracted to work with during 2023- 2025. This will be the last report from IPA, since Sida has decided not to continue the cooperation with IPA.
The incoming report that covers 2023 - 2025) describes the different innovative ideas and methods to reduce poverty in the world and notable in the countries in which they are operating.
Below are main example of innovative methods to reduce poverty:
Embedded Labs Portfolio The size of the embedded labs have expanded: they grew from 22 labs across 14 countries and eight sectors.
The embedded labs go through 5 phases, with the 5th phase being the exit phase. From scoping cultivating support, to proof of concept, then learning by doing and then lab as an institution.
The best bets initiative which focuses on the most promising emerging innovations that have the greatest potential to scale. All prioritised Best Bets from 2024 advanced along the path to scale.
Launching of major new research initiatives: the world's first research for displaced population has been launched.
Example of results mentioned in the report:
- Dissemination event of results in Zambia (2400 children) Small-Quantity Lipid-Based Nutrient Supplements (SQ-LNS) impact on stunting: ready-to-eat nutritional packets that improve child growth have shown strong potential for nationwide impact in Zambia. IPA is now working with the Ministry of Health to define a government-led delivery model for SQ-LNS at scale.
- Cognitive behavioral therapy to reduce crime: Urban crime and violence is one of the most costly and divisive issues facing cities around the world. Short-term studies have demonstrated that cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), a therapeutic approach to improving a wide range of harmful beliefs and behaviors, is an effective way to reduce violence and criminality among adolescents and young adults. To understand the long-term effectiveness of CBT among adults, researchers evaluated the impact of a short-term CBT program and the distribution of unconditional cash transfers on the behavior of high-risk young men in Liberia. Results demonstrated that CBT reduced criminal behavior among participants both in the short run, one year following the intervention, and the long run, ten years later. At both intervals, these results were greater for participants who received both CBT and cash grants, but cash grants alone had no impact. FID (final investment decision) approval to scale the innovative concept in Liberia.
- Becoming One (BI): Couples counseling to reduce IPV (intimate partner violence): Scale-up of Becoming One in Uganda with World Vision, Church of Uganda, and ICM (international confederation of midwifes); Workshop and pilot to adapt and test B1 in Kenya.
- Published Multigenerational Perspective on Childcare review;
Financial report 2023 - 2025
IPA has been affected by the termination of the USAID grant.
Since the initial stop work orders were received in January 2025, IPA took action to reduce both fixed costs and variable country office costs by cutting all discretionary expenses (non-essential travel and meeting expenses, transition to a new intranet, implementation of a new system for direct payments). They have also reduced some staff to part time or reduced salary, paused recruitment for roles that are not absolutely essential for business continuity, and eliminated 15 global staff positions along with 13 project staff and over 100 enumerators. IPA has had to work in a more leand and efficient way.
Sida has provided core support to IPA - and thanks to the core support IPA has been able to continue its main operations during 2025.
The final financial report show that the estimated revenue during the period of the grant was approximately $161.7 million USD. Sida's contribution of $3.87 million USD was approximately 2.4% of IPA's budget during that time.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
